title: Why Your Fingers Wrinkle but Your Face Doesn't
description:
Why do your fingers wrinkle in water, but your face doesn't? It isn't the water soaking in: when the nerve to a finger is damaged, that finger stays smooth. Your nerves tell tiny blood vessels under the skin to shrink, and the skin folds into grooves. In 2013, scientists in England found people moved wet marbles 12% faster with wrinkly fingers. Then a team in Berlin tried again and found no difference. The wrinkles are real; why we have them is still an argument.

Grooves for grip, or a fluke? What do you think?

More true whys: https://www.youtube.com/@truewhys?sub_confirmation=1

Sources: Newcastle University (2013) and Kareklas, Nettle & Smulders, Biology Letters 2013; Haseleu et al., PLoS ONE 2014; Changizi et al., Brain, Behavior and Evolution 2011; Smithsonian Magazine, "Why Do We Get Prune Fingers?" (2015).
Animation, music and sound: TrueWhys (original). Fonts: Lilita One (Open Font License).
